extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community (investigators, applicants, institutional administrators, and reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: News summaries and updates about NIH grants policies, processes, resources, and review procedures intended to inform applicants, institutions, and reviewers about changes and reminders affecting extramural research funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model selection appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.” Emphasizes choosing scientifically sound models that fit the research question and, where relevant, favor human-relevant/translational approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan required elements (2026 Pilot format)
rubrics_metrics.description: We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants preparing DMS Plans should use the 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format and include the specified (simplified) required elements. The announcement signals a change in required elements and format that applicants must follow when submitting their DMS Plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding replication and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Embedding replication and reproducibility throughout NIH research is expected and supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “The reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science and to ensuring that findings can benefit patients and communities. NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility. In support of this plan, NIH has launched a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise.” Implication: applications, awards, and institutional practices should consider and promote replication and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring designation: 'Competitive But Not Discussed' (CBND)
rubrics_metrics.description: Middle-third designation for applications: 'competitive but not discussed'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as ‘competitive but not discussed.’” This explains a review/process metric used after emergency modifications to review: applications falling in the middle third are labeled CBND and may not be discussed despite competitiveness; applicants should understand this classification when interpreting review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects: application format and linked awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH released a 6-minute video overview for the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure. Applicants should follow the specified application format for PF5 and be aware that applications may be split into linked awards after review and prior to Just-in-Time requests — plan proposals and budgets accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized peer review goals and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Centralization of NIH peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) aims to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “In March 2025, NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) ... As the one-year anniversary approaches, we are providing an update on the consolidation and its initial effects on the peer-review process.” Applicants and institutions should be aware that review processes and timelines may change due to centralization, with intended impacts on efficiency, competition, and transparency.
